summary: M4-S02 (sla) built five declared artefacts - two EntitlementProcess files, one shared 'First Response' MilestoneType, milestone-completion-decision.md and package.xml - plus an undeclared deploy-order.md. check-outputs returned ok:true and all four XML files parse. The step ends BLOCKED on ambiguity: the step's own declared acceptance-test checker exits 1 under --strict on two W4 findings ('neither <timeTriggers> nor <successActions>'). Clearing W4 requires a WorkflowAlert or WorkflowFieldUpdate, and no step in this plan builds a Workflow file while no clarification names a milestone notification's recipient, offset, sender or template. The two repairs that would pass were built on scratch copies outside the build directory and rejected: one names a component that exists nowhere (deploy failure), the other uses an action-less timeTrigger shape the skill does not document - and the checker cannot tell them apart.

process_observations.observation: The calendar cross-reference --strict was added for is green: at build scope both processes and both milestone overrides resolve 'US Support' against a real <name> in M4-S01's settings file, so all four step-scope W6 findings clear and no W3 replaces them.

The whole documented ERROR set is clean on first write - E1 minutesToComplete positive int, E2 no duplicate version defaults, E3 workflowTimeTriggerUnit enum, E4 SObjectType and recurrenceType enums - and every element written traces to a fenced example in the cited skill's metadata-examples.md.

--strict was added to the acceptance test to promote W3 (the calendar cross-reference) into an assertion, and it collaterally promotes W4, which this plan cannot satisfy because no step anywhere in M1-M5 declares a workflows/ output.

An EMEA-region case will count its first-response milestone on US Support hours (08:00-20:00 New York) while its escalation timer counts on EMEA Support hours via businessHoursSource=Case, so the two SLA clocks on one case pause on different holidays - the exact divergence business-hours gotcha #5 exists to prevent.

No step in this plan owns settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml, so enableEntitlements - the master switch without which every file in this step is inert - and enableMilestoneStoppedTime are unscoped.
This build's package.xml files are split across two API versions - nine at 62.0 and, with this one, four at 67.0 - with no api_version key in plan.json to settle it.

Nothing in this build converts '1 business day' into minutes; 720 was derived as one full US Support open day (08:00-20:00) and 480 (a conventional 8-hour day) and a next-business-day promise are both defensible readings with no source.

The declared file names First_Response_Premier/_Standard are mixed case, while the guide derives an EntitlementProcess file name as slaProcess.NameNorm - the lowercase form of <name> - so a retrieve would return first_response_premier.entitlementProcess-meta.xml instead.

No clarification covers entitlement-process activation, so these processes ship active while M4-S04's escalation rule ships inactive under Q47 - the build's two SLA engines go live on different switches.
An entitlement-and-milestone designer could adjudicate the one-calendar-per-process tension against Q51's Case-calendar authority without re-planning the build.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because the process-versus-Case calendar choice is an SLA design decision this build-time builder is forbidden to make and the plan does not bind.
